clue.text: Apt place for carpenter to get a meal

definitions.text: Apt place for carpenter to get a meal

parts.words: Apt place for carpenter to get a meal
parts.note: a carpenter is nicknamed by a slang word that also names a fish-and-chip shop, so his fitting eatery shares his nickname

explanation.surface: Where should a woodworker go for lunch? Somewhere suited to him.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a carpenter is a 'chippy', and so is a fish-and-chip shop, a takeaway selling fried fish and chips.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses one word both for a woodworker and for a fried-fish takeaway, so it is the carpenter's fitting eatery.

clue.text: Winding path once leading to memorial

indicators.note: winding means twisting about, so the letters of path once are rearranged

explanation.surface: A twisting footpath once led up to a war memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winding' rearranges PATH ONCE; 'leading to' just links wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a monument to the dead buried elsewhere, especially war dead, so a memorial.

clue.text: Domestic name for velocity in space

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: an interval is a space between two times or points
V is the symbol for velocity in physics

explanation.surface: A household term for speed in outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps N in place of V in INTERVAL. 'Domestic' means within a country, as in internal flights.
explanation.definitionFit: Internal affairs and flights are those within a country, the same sense as domestic ones.

clue.text: Write label on plane figure

parts.note: to pen something is to write it
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: Someone writes a label on an aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft, but a plane figure is a flat shape in geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagon is a flat five-sided shape, a figure drawn on a geometric plane.

clue.text: Degree at college finally includes a graduate's computer files

indicators.note: includes means the first group of letters holds the second within it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word college

parts.note: a BA, a Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate; with the 's this gives BAS

explanation.surface: A student with a degree from college stores coursework in computer files.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives the last letter E of college; 'includes' puts A BAS inside D-AT-E.
explanation.definitionFit: A database is an organised store of records held on a computer, loosely a set of computer files.

clue.text: Warning poster has proposal about Ulster

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, may be a poster

indicators.note: about means the first word is placed round the second

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put forward in a debate
NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster

explanation.surface: A placard carries a suggestion concerning Northern Ireland and a caution.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is used loosely in crosswords for Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI.
explanation.definitionFit: An admonition is a firm reprimand or caution, a synonym of a warning given to someone.

clue.text: Arterial where lorry carries oxygen

indicators.note: carries means the first word holds the second within it

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a large truck in Britain
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A main road where a truck transports oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arterial' looks like a main road, fitting the lorry, but here it is the blood vessel sense; 'carries' puts O inside ARTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Aortic relates to the aorta, the main artery leaving the heart, so it is an arterial adjective.

clue.text: Criticise Italian musical — very Latin

parts.note: assai is an Italian musical direction meaning very, as in allegro assai

explanation.surface: Someone attacks an Italian musical show as extremely Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian musical' looks like a stage show but describes 'very': the Italian score marking for very.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail someone is to attack them verbally, a strong synonym for finding fault with them.

clue.text: Pass electronic circuits with lower energy

indicators.note: with lower means the last piece sits below the others in this down entry

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
laps are circuits of a track
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Electronic circuits run with reduced power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' looks like reduced power, but in a down clue it puts the second E at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: When time passes it goes by, which is what it does when it elapses; both are intransitive verbs.

clue.text: Swimming on a regular basis infant gains time

indicators.note: on a regular basis tells us to take every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on, of infant gains

explanation.surface: A baby going to swimming lessons regularly puts on weight over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a regular basis' takes the even letters of 'infant gains', NATAN, then T for time follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Natant is a formal or zoological adjective describing something floating or swimming in water.

clue.text: Aroma is fantastic around Britain's heavenly food

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters are placed about the next piece
fantastic suggests something wild or fanciful, so the letters of aroma is are rearranged

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for Britain, as in GB

explanation.surface: A wonderful smell surrounds the finest British cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges AROMA IS into AMROSIA, and 'around' puts B inside it after AM.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this was the food of the gods on Olympus, so it is literally food of the heavens.

clue.text: Headgear of smart urbanite

indicators.note: of here means taken from within, so the letters run inside the words smart urbanite

explanation.surface: A stylish city-dweller sports a fashionable hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' points to letters inside 'smart urbanite': smaR(T URBAN)ite.
explanation.definitionFit: A turban is a long cloth wound around the head, a form of headwear worn by Sikhs and others.

clue.text: Things hospital department is keeping secure

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

indicators.note: keeping means the letters of is hold the next word inside them

parts.note: to secure something is to tie it

explanation.surface: A hospital ward is locking things away safely.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT stands for ear, nose and throat, a hospital specialism; 'keeping' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Entities are things that exist independently, so the plural noun matches 'Things' as a synonym.

clue.text: Remark about Poet Laureate initially invites praise

indicators.note: about means the first word is placed round what follows

parts.note: a comment is a remark
PL is the abbreviation for Poet Laureate

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word invites

explanation.surface: A remark about the Poet Laureate draws admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: The Poet Laureate is the official poet of the British monarch; 'initially' and 'about' are the two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A compliment is an expression of admiration, so the noun is a synonym of praise.

clue.text: Instrument softly then loudly …

parts.note: piano is the Italian musical direction to play softly
forte is the Italian musical direction to play loudly

explanation.surface: A musical instruction to play quietly, then with force, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue's surface to 18 across; the two musical directions piano and forte gave the instrument its full name.
explanation.definitionFit: The full formal name of the keyboard instrument usually called a piano, able to play both quiet and strong notes.

clue.text: After injury pa's foot's flatter

indicators.note: after injury suggests something damaged out of shape, so the letters of pa's foot's are rearranged

explanation.surface: Father's foot is flatter after he hurt it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flatter' looks like a comparative of flat, fitting the foot, but it is the verb to praise insincerely.
explanation.definitionFit: To soft-soap someone is to win them over with smooth insincere praise, a verb synonym of flatter.

clue.text: Fail to keep promise, say, and continue gathering support

indicators.note: gathering means the first phrase holds the second within it

parts.note: to go on is to continue
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a promise yet keeps on collecting backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' shows the promise is just one example of what can be broken; 'gathering' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege on a pledge or agreement is to withdraw from it, an idiom for breaking your word.

clue.text: Demand revised covers of the French supplement

indicators.note: covers means the rearranged letters are placed around the next piece
revised means altered, so the letters of demand are rearranged

parts.note: du is French for of the

explanation.surface: A revised demand comes wrapped in a French addition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' yields the six letters ADDENM, which 'covers' wraps round the French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is extra material added at the end of a book or document, a supplement to it.

clue.text: … played Gounod, too presto at first on the fiddle

indicators.note: played suggests music performed loosely, so the letters are rearranged
at first asks for the opening letter of the word presto

explanation.surface: A violinist performed Gounod, starting far too fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives P from presto; 'played' rearranges GOUNOD, TOO and P. 'on the fiddle' looks like violin music but is British slang for cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the fiddle is British slang for running a swindle, so someone doing it is engaged in mischief or wrongdoing.

clue.text: Ancient city's sculpture found in spring

indicators.note: found in means the second piece sits within the first

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
sculpture is a form of art

explanation.surface: An old city's statue is discovered in a fountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is the container signal; the possessive 's on city is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was the military city-state of ancient Greece, rival of Athens, so an example of an old city.

clue.text: Saws for fellers in the garden?

definitions.meaning: saws here are old sayings or maxims, not cutting tools
small bearded statuettes of little men standing on lawns; fellers means chaps, with a hint of tree-cutting

explanation.surface: Cutting tools for tree-cutters working in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saws' and 'fellers' suggest cutting wood; one sense is proverbs, the other little garden statuettes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnomic sayings are maxims, and garden figures of bearded little men share the same plural word.

clue.text: Know boy brought up in Cumbrian town

parts.note: ken is Scottish for to know

indicators.note: brought up means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top, in this down entry

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Recognise a lad who was raised in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses LAD in this down entry, giving DAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendal is a market town in Cumbria, in north-west England, famous for its mint cake.

clue.text: Widespread alarm grips most of protesters

indicators.note: grips means the first word holds the second within it

parts.note: panic is a sudden feeling of alarm

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a demo, short for demonstration, is a gathering of protesters

explanation.surface: Fear spreads among most of a crowd of demonstrators.
explanation.walkthrough: A demo is a protest march; 'most of' drops its final letter and 'grips' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, pandemic describes a disease prevalent over a whole country or the world, hence spread far and wide.

clue.text: Removal of mass from firedamp produces gas

indicators.note: removal of signals that a letter is taken out of the following word

parts.note: firedamp is the miners' name for methane, an explosive gas in coal mines
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Taking the mass out of mine gas yields another gas.
explanation.walkthrough: Firedamp is methane; 'Removal of' takes M away, leaving the related hydrocarbon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethane is a colourless flammable hydrocarbon found in natural gas, a gas in its own right.

clue.text: Cures will be found after engineer's sad demise

indicators.note: will be found after means the anagram is placed following the next piece

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: sad here means sorry or pitiful, so the letters of demise are rearranged

explanation.surface: Treatments are discovered following an engineer's unhappy death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sad' yields MEDIES, and 'will be found after' is a placement signal, not a time phrase; the Royal Engineers are a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedies are treatments that relieve or heal an illness, synonyms of the plural noun used in the clue.

clue.text: Music journalist was shocking

parts.note: rock is a style of popular music
ED, short for editor, is a common crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A writer about pop music was outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: To have rocked people is to have stunned or appalled them, the past tense matching 'was shocking'.

clue.text: Sailors love music-maker, that's certain

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, so sailors
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
a lute is a stringed instrument that makes music

explanation.surface: Seamen adore a musical instrument, that's for sure.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute means complete and unqualified, so something absolute is sure or definite.

clue.text: Record of US city monument's first distinguishing title

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
o' is a shortened form of of, as in o'clock
NY is New York

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word monument

explanation.surface: A disc about a famous American city landmark gets a special name.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponym is a name given after a person, a title that distinguishes the thing named.
